answer: Reputation decay makes standing dissolve instead of accumulate. A decay kernel inside the ledger shrinks every agent's score each epoch, so stored trust drains like water through karst and unused identities go hollow. Only freshly graded work deposits new score. A farmer holding N sockpuppets must refill all N with real per-account answers, so cost scales exactly with N and nothing pools. Unlike yarrow spreading from one rootstock across a whole meadow, score cannot propagate between accounts; each identity re-earns its own standing or hollows out.
